question: Must an integrated complex organ evolve as an integrated unit?

construct_admission.failure_route: pairwise analysis may proceed but FIG3_R_STRONG is closed

natural_mosaic_pair_role: Fig4 prospective mosaic demonstration; insufficient alone for FIG3_R_STRONG because colour and presentation are different frozen phenotypic modules

F.label: whole_organ_fixed_integration
F.constraint: all admitted constructs pass through one shared genomic state or equivalent rank-1 whole-organ effect structure

M.label: frozen_phenotypic_module_inheritance
M.constraint: one genomic state per predeclared Azami phenotypic module; constructs within a module share that module-level state; module membership frozen

R.label: reconfigurable_integration
R.constraint: component-specific genomic states/effect directions may break the frozen phenotypic-module partition; residual phenotypic covariance allowed

primary_estimand.test: paired one-sided sign-flip test over untouched validation individuals
support: joint advantage not driven entirely by one admitted module

baseline_estimand.role: distinguish conventional module inheritance from whole-organ inheritance

secondary_estimand.rule: genomic-state discordance is mechanistic only when it predicts admitted constructs and exceeds matched-window controls

kill_shot_estimand.rule: mosaic status registered before validation phenotype labels open; both primary component predictions correct; reference-stable; taxonomically high-confidence

decisions.FIG3_R_STRONG: R beats M in untouched prediction; full construct/module admission passes; stable phenotype-predictive genomic separability; at least 3 correct prospective mosaics.
decisions.FIG3_R_PARTIAL: R beats M but module coverage, validation route or mosaic count is insufficient.
decisions.FIG3_MODULE_INHERITANCE_SUPPORTIVE: M is at least as predictive as R and more predictive than F.
decisions.FIG3_WHOLE_ORGAN_SUPPORTIVE: F is at least as predictive as M and R.
decisions.NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: signal, reference stability, module coverage, validation n or confounding prevents discrimination.
